title: Astrology and Christianity: Can They Coexist?
dek: An in-depth theological exploration of the relationship between Christian faith, personal free will, divination, and the study of the heavens.
author: Rev. Adam Ian Stratmeyer & CA Editorial
content: For centuries, Christians have been taught to shy away from anything resembling the stars. Yet Scripture begins not with a condemnation of the heavens, but with their intentional creation: 'And God said, Let there be lights in the firmament of the heaven... and let them be for signs, and for seasons, and for days, and years' (Genesis 1:14).
Notice the very first purpose assigned to the celestial bodies by the Creator Himself: they are for signs (Hebrew: Ototh — heralds, tokens, divine markers).

The critical theological distinction lies between divination (idolatrous worship of the created over the Creator, or claiming fatalistic control over destiny) and biblical contemplation (reading God's celestial clockwork and general revelation). The heavens do not compel human action; rather, 'The heavens declare the glory of God; and the firmament sheweth his handywork' (Psalm 19:1).

As an ecumenical ministry ordained under the Universal Life Church, we invite believers—Evangelicals, Catholics, Mainline Protestants, and seekers alike—to reclaim the sacred heavens as God's majestic canvas without fear or condemnation.

title: What Does the Bible Really Say About the Stars & The Mazzaroth?
dek: Discover what the Bible says about celestial signs, the meaning of Job's Mazzaroth, and the Star of Bethlehem that guided the Magi.
author: Universal Life Church Ministry Guild
content: In the book of Job—one of the oldest texts in the biblical canon—God Himself speaks directly from the whirlwind, challenging Job with the mechanics of the cosmos: 'Canst thou bind the sweet influences of Pleiades, or loose the bands of Orion? Canst thou bring forth Mazzaroth in his season? or canst thou guide Arcturus with his sons?' (Job 38:31-32).

The word Mazzaroth (מַזָּרוֹת) refers specifically to the twelve signs of the zodiac and their associated constellations. God does not condemn the Mazzaroth; He claims authorship and sovereignty over it.

Furthermore, when Jesus Christ was born in Bethlehem, who were the very first human beings to recognize the cosmic timing of His birth? Not the religious scribes in Jerusalem, but the Magi—astronomers and celestial scholars from the East who observed His star in the heavens (Matthew 2:2).
Christian astrology is not about superstition; it is about recognizing the harmony of God's cosmos and understanding that every star was numbered and named by our Heavenly Father (Psalm 147:4).

title: The Christian Zodiac: Finding Christ's Gospel in the Heavens
dek: How early church scholars and 19th-century theologians discovered the prophetic story of redemption mapped across the 12 signs.
author: Rev. Adam Ian Stratmeyer
content: Long before the written scriptures were codified on parchment, ancient believers looked up into the night sky to remember the promises of God. Scholars such as Frances Rolleston, Joseph Seiss (The Gospel in the Stars), and E.W. Bullinger demonstrated that the 12 signs tell an orderly story of redemption.

The cycle begins in Virgo (Betulah, the Virgin bearing the Promised Seed, Isaiah 7:14) and concludes triumphantly in Leo (Aryeh, the Lion of the Tribe of Judah conquering the ancient adversary, Revelation 5:5).

Between these two celestial poles lies the entire gospel narrative: the price paid in Libra, the spiritual warfare of Scorpio trampled by the Redeemer, the sacrifice of the goat in Capricorn yielding living fish, and the living water poured out in Aquarius.
When understood through this Christocentric lens, the stars cease to be a source of pagan confusion and become a profound testament of praise.

title: The Biblical & Spiritual Meaning of Your Birth Month
dek: Explore the prophetic Hebrew calendar connections, tribal blessings, and spiritual gifts associated with your season of birth.
author: CA Editorial Board
content: In biblical tradition, time is holy. The biblical Hebrew calendar is lunisolar, with each month beginning with the new moon (Rosh Chodesh) and aligning with a specific tribe of Israel and constellation sign.

When you were born into this world, God placed you at an exact intersection of time, season, and celestial alignment. 'Before I formed thee in the belly I knew thee; and before thou camest forth out of the womb I sanctified thee' (Jeremiah 1:5).

Whether born in Nisan (associated with Aries and Judah's praise), Tishrei (associated with Libra and divine reconciliation), or Adar (associated with Pisces and the joyful turning of mourning into gladness), your life reflects God's deliberate design.
Explore your birth placement not as a rigid fate, but as a personalized tapestry of spiritual gifts, temperament strengths, and prayer focuses.
